key_insight: Magnetic fields control hydrogel balloon shape and swelling stability, with sufficiently strong fields restricting stable swollen states to a bounded pressure window.
engineering_relevance: The results inform magnetically controlled soft-device design by identifying swelling-induced burst risks and transient stresses that equilibrium analysis can miss.
method: Couple finite-strain Ogden elasticity, Flory–Huggins solvent mixing, and magnetic free energy.
Solve transient diffusion and large deformation using nonlinear FEM, a staggered scheme, and Taylor–Hood-type discretisation.
Track pressurised balloons under one or two current-carrying coils from dry inflation to swollen equilibrium or burst.
evidence_signal: The formulation recovers analytical free-swelling stretch and delayed bursting, agrees with equilibrium energy minimisation at converged states, and predicts transient membrane stresses nearly an order of magnitude above equilibrium values.
watch_item: The abstract reports analytical and equilibrium consistency checks but no experimental validation; predicted burst boundaries warrant physical testing.
paper_title: A nonlinear transient finite element analysis of coupled solvent diffusion and large deformation of magneto-elastic hydrogel balloon
